endings.name: The Charter
endings.summary: The final match is signed at 4-4. Alexi and the princess write terms between a god and the people who sail: lanes kept calm, wild water left wild. Cost: the tab becomes a schedule of the terms, every pledge in it a clause he keeps for good, and the toll is read out on the terms' last page as the reason for the lanes.

endings.name: Paid in Kind
endings.summary: After a win, with all eight chits pinned to what they bought, he unsigns them at the tideline: eight counter-clockwise stirs, each taking a tier off the rose ring for good. The Company's claim on the sea is gone; what it built and pays for stays. He is a god who owes nothing and can raise a ripple. Cost: he can never dive for anyone again, the wild regions stay as wild as the player left them, and the toll is entered as “outstanding, for ever”.

endings.name: No Lord
endings.summary: Alexi beats the Lord of Tea and gives up the sea, which was not meant to be owned by anyone. He becomes a mortal sailor; the Company's charters and its lights fall. Cost: the debtor ceases to exist, so the debt dies with him, and so does anyone who could answer for the drowned; the epilogue lists, region by region, where wrecks will now come back with no one to answer to.

endings.name: The Wild Sea
endings.summary: Alexi beats the Lord of Tea and keeps the sea, and repudiates the tab. He is the god again; the hymns come back, and so do the wrecks. Cost: the surety is called, and the princess leaves the boat to go ashore and face it for her father's house; the toll is sung to the hymn's tune, by name.

endings.name: The Lord's Peace
endings.summary: The Lord of Tea owns every ship that sails. The sea is safe, and Alexi is a man on an old boat whose tide no longer answers. Cost: he took the salary, or lost the board; the last bottle is Company issue; the Wreck Book closes, and so does every hymn.
